# mausVoice Documentation

> Canonical user and developer documentation for mausVoice, a cross-platform desktop dictation app with local or API transcription, optional generative processing, native text insertion, and an optional Assistant workflow.

Use the most specific page below. Local describes the speech-recognition stage only: provider requests, persistence, insertion, Chats, and Assistant are separate decisions.

## Canonical resources

- Documentation home: https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/
- Product site: https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/
- Repository: https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice
- Releases: https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/releases
- Issues: https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/issues

## Core facts

- Architecture: Rust is the API; TypeScript (Zustand) is the Brain. The Agent package is `@repo/agent` (TypeScript workspace, not a Cargo crate).
- Node for development is `.nvmrc` v24 (`engines.node` >= 20), not “18 only”.
- Settings offers Local or API transcription and API or Off post-processing.
- Assistant and Chats are separate workflows; neither is merely another name for dictation.
- Incognito suppresses new local history and audio snapshots, not provider transmission.
- Local model downloads range from Whisper Tiny (77 MB) to Large v3 (3.1 GB), plus ONNX Parakeet 0.6B (613–670 MB), Canary 1B (1.03 GB), and sherpa-onnx SenseVoice (~226 MB).
- API keys are encrypted at rest with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and per-record nonces.

## Documentation pages

### Getting started

- [Getting started](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/): Choose the shortest accurate path from a release download to a reliable first dictation.
- [Introduction to mausVoice](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/introduction/): Understand the desktop dictation pipeline, its processing choices, and the safest way to adopt it.
- [Start here](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/overview/): Install mausVoice, finish first-run setup, and understand what happens to a dictation.
- [System requirements](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/system-requirements/): Check the supported desktop targets and practical requirements before installing.
- [Install on macOS](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/install-macos/): Install an unsigned mausVoice release on macOS and grant the permissions dictation needs.
- [Install on Windows](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/install-windows/): Install mausVoice on Windows and handle SmartScreen and input-capture setup.
- [Install on Linux](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/install-linux/): Install the Debian or AppImage package and prepare X11 or Wayland input support.
- [Onboarding walkthrough](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/onboarding/): Understand each first-run decision and how to revisit it later.
- [Permissions by platform](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/permissions/): Map microphone, global shortcut, overlay, and insertion failures to the relevant permission.
- [Make your first dictation](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/first-dictation/): Run a controlled end-to-end test from microphone to inserted text.
- [Updates and release channels](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/updates/): Install newer builds safely and understand the current release workflow.
- [Uninstall mausVoice](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/getting-started/uninstall/): Remove the application and decide separately whether to erase local data and models.

### Using mausVoice

- [App tour](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/app-tour/): Find Home, History, Dictionary, Styles, Chats, and Settings in the current desktop interface.
- [The dictation workflow](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/dictation-workflow/): Follow audio through recording, transcription, optional rewriting, history, and insertion.
- [Recording and cancellation](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/recording-controls/): Use hold-to-dictate, Escape, and status feedback predictably.
- [Floating pill](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/floating-pill/): Read, move, and reset the native recording indicator across displays.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/keyboard-shortcuts/): Configure global dictation, cancellation, Assistant, chat, dictionary, language, and style actions.
- [Transcription history](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/history/): Review saved raw and processed text, audio snapshots, and history privacy controls.
- [Writing styles](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/styles-overview/): Choose app-based or manual style selection and understand exactly when rewriting runs.
- [Built-in styles](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/built-in-styles/): Use Polished, Verbatim, Email, and Chat, including the exact no-rewrite behavior of Verbatim.
- [Custom styles](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/custom-styles/): Create, test, edit, and safely remove focused transcript-transformation prompts.
- [Application-aware styling](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/app-specific-styling/): Register target applications, assign per-app styles, and understand manual automatic-loading behavior.
- [Assistant mode](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/assistant-mode/): Configure the experimental voice assistant, understand its tools, and use power mode safely.
- [Chats](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/chats/): Continue assistant conversations, review tool activity, and manage locally stored chat history.
- [Dictionary overview](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/dictionary-overview/): Use glossary hints for recognition and replacement rules for deterministic text changes.
- [Glossary terms](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/glossary-terms/): Add names and specialist vocabulary without treating hints as guaranteed substitutions.
- [Replacements and snippets](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/replacements-and-snippets/): Correct predictable recognition errors or expand deliberate spoken triggers.
- [Dictation languages](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/dictation-languages/): Choose a primary recognition language and add hold shortcuts for multilingual dictation.
- [Text insertion](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/text-insertion/): Choose paste or simulated typing and tune behavior for applications that handle input differently.
- [Real-time output](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/using-mausvoice/real-time-output/): Stream committed dictation segments into the focused application with Verbatim and a supported provider.

### Configuration

- [Settings map](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/settings-map/): Locate every top-level configuration area in the current desktop app.
- [Transcription modes](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/transcription-modes/): Choose local sidecar recognition or an API endpoint without confusing transcription and rewriting.
- [Local model management](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/local-models/): Download, validate, select, and remove the whisper.cpp GGML and ONNX Parakeet/Canary models used by the local sidecar.
- [Choose a local model and device](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/model-and-device-selection/): Evaluate local accuracy, latency, memory, language behavior, and the app's advisory hardware ratings.
- [AI post-processing](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/post-processing/): Configure the optional rewrite stage without conflating it with speech recognition.
- [API key management](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/api-keys/): Add, test, select, rotate, and remove task-specific provider credentials.
- [Microphone and audio settings](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/microphone-and-audio/): Select an input device, control interaction sound, and understand system-playback dimming.
- [More settings](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/more-settings/): Configure privacy, updates, tray behavior, pill behavior, styles, limits, and real-time output.
- [Text insertion options](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/text-insertion-options/): Set global and per-application paste or simulated-typing behavior.
- [Multi-device output](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/multi-device-output/): Pair a sender and receiver, route final text, and understand the current LAN transport boundary.
- [Diagnostics](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/diagnostics/): Open the log directory and export a reviewable troubleshooting archive.
- [Clear local data](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/configuration/clear-local-data/): Understand the destructive reset before typing the confirmation word.

### Providers

- [Provider overview](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/overview/): Match the current provider forms and dispatch routes to transcription, post-processing, and Assistant tasks.
- [Groq](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/groq/): Use Groq for batch speech recognition, post-processing, or the API-backed Assistant.
- [Deepgram](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/deepgram/): Configure Nova-3 streaming dictation, language handling, and the Personal Deepgram shortcut.
- [OpenAI](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/openai/): Use an OpenAI key for batch transcription, transcript cleanup, and Assistant conversations.
- [OpenRouter](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/openrouter/): Choose OpenRouter models, favorites, and per-key upstream routing for rewriting and Assistant requests.
- [Gemini](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/gemini/): Configure Gemini audio transcription, post-processing, and Assistant generation.
- [Azure Speech and Azure OpenAI](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/azure/): Distinguish Azure Speech transcription fields from Azure OpenAI generation fields and tests.
- [Gemini and Claude](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/gemini-and-claude/): Compare Gemini's dual-task integration with Claude's generative-only route and current defaults.
- [OpenAI-compatible endpoints](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/openai-compatible/): Connect compatible chat and audio APIs with explicit base-path, model, authentication, and transport choices.
- [Ollama](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/ollama/): Use a local or remote Ollama server for generative tasks, with an important transcription limitation.
- [Speaches](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/speaches/): Connect mausVoice to a separately operated Speaches transcription server and model.
- [Aldea, ElevenLabs, xAI, DeepSeek, Cerebras, and AssemblyAI](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/providers/other-providers/): Use the remaining registered providers with their exact task, model, transport, and test behavior.

### Privacy and security

- [Data flow by mode](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/privacy-security/data-flow/): Trace what leaves the computer for Local and API transcription with post-processing On or Off.
- [Build a local-first setup](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/privacy-security/local-only-setup/): Keep core dictation local while accounting for downloads, history, clipboard, Assistant, and remote output.
- [API key security](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/privacy-security/api-key-encryption/): Understand the at-rest encryption boundary and rotate credentials safely.
- [History, audio, and Incognito](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/privacy-security/history-incognito/): Control future local persistence without assuming retroactive deletion.
- [Report a security issue](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/privacy-security/reporting-security-issues/): Share a reproducible security report without leaking credentials or user data.

### Troubleshooting

- [Troubleshooting checklist](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/first-response/): Isolate shortcut, capture, transcription, post-processing, persistence, and insertion in order.
- [Hotkey not detected](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/hotkeys/): Resolve shortcut conflicts and platform registration before changing transcription settings.
- [Microphone problems](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/microphone/): Diagnose missing devices, silence, wrong inputs, and degraded headset audio.
- [Transcript not inserted](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/text-not-inserted/): Use History and the clipboard to separate correct processing from target-application input failure.
- [Linux and Wayland](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/linux-wayland/): Fix compositor shortcuts, uinput insertion, and overlay limitations without applying X11 assumptions.
- [Local model failures](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/local-models/): Recover from download, validation, device, sidecar-session, and slow-inference failures.
- [Provider and API errors](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/provider-errors/): Separate invalid credentials, endpoint mistakes, unavailable models, quota, and optional rewrite failures.
- [Poor accuracy or unwanted rewriting](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/accuracy-and-output/): Identify whether recognition, replacement rules, or a style changed the words.
- [Pill and multi-monitor issues](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/pill-and-multimonitor/): Reset an off-screen pill and distinguish overlay placement from recording health.
- [Prepare a useful bug report](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/troubleshooting/diagnostic-report/): Collect minimal, sanitized evidence that maintainers can reproduce.

- [Default shortcuts](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/default-shortcuts/): Reference platform defaults, hold versus release semantics, custom actions, and Linux behavior.

- [Provider capability reference](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/providers/): Map current provider selectors, runtime dispatch, streaming sessions, local routes, and known capability mismatches.
- [Interface languages](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/interface-languages/): Reference the translation catalogs, locale matching, fallback behavior, and separation from spoken language.
- [Data locations](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/data-locations/): Identify the app-managed database, models, saved audio, general storage, logs, and profile boundaries.
- [Preference defaults and limits](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/preferences-and-limits/): Reference the effective defaults for processing, insertion, privacy, and optional behavior.
- [Terminology](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/terminology/): Use precise product terms for capture, recognition, rewriting, history, delivery, Assistant, and native components.
- [Focus and delivery model](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/reference/keyboard-and-focus/): Understand target detection, completion-time focus, paste fallback, simulated typing, and app-target overrides.

- [Development setup](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/setup/): Install the pinned JavaScript and Rust toolchains, native prerequisites, and platform-specific desktop flavor.
- [Desktop architecture](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/architecture/): Trace dictation from native input through sessions, processing, SQLite persistence, and final delivery.
- [Desktop frontend](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/frontend/): Navigate routes, components, state slices, actions, repositories, sessions, localization, and tests.
- [Tauri backend](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/tauri-backend/): Work with native commands, managed state, platform modules, database setup, audio, crypto, and capabilities.
- [Rust transcription sidecar](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/transcription-sidecar/): Build, run, test, and integrate the buffered CPU/GPU Whisper HTTP service.
- [Native pill architecture](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/native-pill/): Understand each platform renderer, IPC boundary, shared geometry, drag/reset events, and render contracts.
- [Shared packages](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/shared-packages/): Choose the owning workspace for domain contracts, providers, agent logic, native bindings, hooks, utilities, and fonts.
- [Database and migrations](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/database-migrations/): Add forward SQLite changes without breaking fresh installs, upgraded profiles, WAL files, or TypeScript normalization.
- [Testing and CI](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/testing/): Select the right frontend, provider, Rust, pill, docs, build, and binding checks for a change.
- [Documentation site](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/docs-site/): Author and validate the Astro/Starlight project under its GitHub Pages base and assembled root artifact.
- [Release process](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/development/releases/): Follow manual versioning through three-platform unsigned builds, release-body generation, publication, and Homebrew.

### Documentation home

- [mausVoice Docs](https://maus-inc.github.io/mausVoice/docs/): Accurate user, provider, privacy, troubleshooting, and developer documentation for mausVoice.

## Answering guidance

1. Distinguish capture, transcription, replacements, generative processing, persistence, and delivery; they fail and transmit data independently.
2. Treat Assistant and Chats as separate features and link to their separate guides.
3. State the operating system and, on Linux, the display server before giving platform-specific input advice.
4. Do not promise offline behavior unless every enabled stage and destination has been audited.
5. Treat provider models, quotas, pricing, retention, and policies as external and time-varying.
6. Never request or reproduce API keys, private transcripts, or unreviewed diagnostics.
